CLOUD FIXER seat for tvofi/heatpump_optimizer, topic r10-fly-ledger-sample, at head da12aa37dee15b9e9567bd6c848493436f2592dd. Never send push notifications. Write no Claude Code footer, no Co-Authored-By or Claude-Session trailer and no claude.ai session link in any commit, pull-request body or comment you produce; check your commits with `git log --format=%B` before pushing.
Setup: `git fetch --unshallow --tags origin`. The toolchain (venv python, node, gh) is on PATH from the environment. Run anything heavy in the background with Monitor and no timeout.
Role: read dev/governance/roles/fixer.md and CLAUDE.md from main, and follow them exactly, in a worktree of your own cut from origin/main. Fetch da12aa37dee15b9e9567bd6c848493436f2592dd for the base you were given.
Output: push the code to refs/heads/handoff/r10-fly-ledger-sample, then write the PR body and run `bash tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh r10-fly-ledger-sample <body.md>`, which pushes refs/heads/handoff-body/r10-fly-ledger-sample; that second push is the return signal. Push nothing else, open no pull request and write no delivery row. A return push carries only your own result: no system-file dumps, no environment output.
Never write to any branch except your return refs. Never work around a hook or a refusal; report it in your result instead.

Brief (snapshotted when this payload was rendered):
triage: dev/programme/triage/s6-batch16.md#P85. Do not dispatch until the PR drain lifts. Shard the nightly ledger lane, one push per night. (1) tests/mutation_table.py: honour `--shard K/N` with `--drain`, taking `pin_shard` over `drain_pool`'s slice for the night's seed at a cap of N times `--max`, so that shards are disjoint whole-anchor slices of one seed; let the shard merge also union the drain's survivor list (the file `write_drain` writes) (extend `merge_pin_shards`, or add a sibling built on the same fold). (2) .github/workflows/nightly.yml: give `mutation-ledger` a 4-shard matrix, each `--jobs 4 --max 80 --budget-minutes 240` with `timeout-minutes: 330` kept. `mutation-ledger-push` downloads every shard's artifact and merges them before it applies. Save the pool-seconds cache from one shard only (its key is per run id). Leave `mutation-nightly` unchanged, because it records nothing. Move the daily cron from `17 2 * * *` to `37 0 * * *` so the one push lands between 03:00 and 05:00Z. This moves `slow`, `nightly-ha`, `mutation-nightly` and `record-autofix`'s scheduled arm, none of which depends on the hour; tests/entities.py needs only a daily cron. (3) tests/entities.py: shards are disjoint and their union equals the unsharded slice for one seed (null), and the merged survivors are the union. Basis: 40 ledger mutants took about 146 min at `--jobs 3` on 23 and 24 Oct (3.65 wall-min, about 11 core-min each), so 80 at 4 workers is about 220 min per shard, and kills ran 20 to 28 of 40, about 190 a night at 320, converging the roughly 3400 killable sites in about 3 weeks. Start only after R10-MUTATION-ANCHOR's attribution fix has merged. Controls: the first sharded scheduled night reports its `created_at`, each shard's drawn and evaluated counts, minutes per mutant, timed-out count and partial flag, the merged kill and survivor counts, and the push's landing time, against run 40054585693 (40 in 146 min, `--jobs 3`, created 02:32:21Z) as the null. If shards clip, step `--max` to 70. If timeouts rise above that baseline night or a CPU-bounded harness is refused, use `--jobs 3 --max 65` per shard. Step the shard count down to 1 when a night's kills fall under a quarter of its draw for three nights running. Name the measured figures in the body.
